overview: The Committee of the Whole held its fourth preliminary budget meeting for fiscal year 2027 to review the proposed budgets for the Assessors, Facilities, Debt Service, Pensions, and Insurance departments.

items.title: 26061 - Annual Budget Process: Assessing Department
items.summary: Chief Assessor Jared Yagjian reported a mostly level-funded budget, noting that a digital flyover software for change detection and new growth identification was not funded but remains a priority for future years.

items.title: 26061 - Annual Budget Process: Facilities Department
items.summary: Facilities Director David McIntyre outlined a strategy to transition from reactive triage to preventative maintenance to control long-term costs. The council discussed custodial contract costs and the planned redesign of the City Council chambers to accommodate four additional members.

items.title: 26061 - Annual Budget Process: Bonds and Interest
items.summary: CFO Bob Dickinson reported that debt service currently accounts for approximately 5% of the general fund, with upcoming costs primarily driven by interest on temporary notes for school HVAC projects.

items.title: 26061 - Annual Budget Process: Pensions
items.summary: The city remains on track to reach full pension funding by 2033, though officials noted the multi-hundred-million-dollar OPEB liability for retiree health insurance remains unfunded.

items.title: 26061 - Annual Budget Process: Workers' Compensation and Insurance
items.summary: Budget increases were attributed to rising medical costs for claimants and a 9% increase in GIC health insurance premiums. The committee requested historical data on workers' compensation settlements to better understand expenditure trends.
